solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Covers large property with grounds in English county

indicators.note: in says the property sits inside the county's abbreviated name

parts.note: BEDS is the short form of Bedfordshire
a spread is a large farm or estate, especially in North America

explanation.surface: An estate agent's listing: a big property with land somewhere in the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDS is the usual short name for Bedfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: bedspreads are the decorative covers laid over a made bed.

clue.text: Bowled, dismissed in match

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
a batter who is dismissed is out

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a batter bowled and out during the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket dismissals are a favourite source of letters: B for bowled, OUT for dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bout is a single contest, such as a boxing or wrestling match.

clue.text: Decline small sweet

definitions.meaning: to decline is to fall or go down
a fruit ... or pear ... is a little boiled sweet

explanation.surface: Someone turning down a tiny candy.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for falling away, and also the name of a small boiled sweet such as a lemon drop.

clue.text: Hierarchy strictly for the birds?

definitions.meaning: a ranking of status within a group
taken literally, the phrase is the order in which hens peck one another

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that rankings are silly, 'for the birds'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the birds' usually means worthless; here it is literal, since the term began with farmyard hens.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names any social ranking, and it was first observed in poultry establishing dominance.

clue.text: Training, after ten, in the Spanish bar

indicators.note: in places the pair of pieces inside the Spanish article

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: after puts the training letters behind the ten

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten
PE is physical education, i.e. physical training

explanation.surface: A workout routine described in a Spanish bar, after ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a place to drink; it is the verb meaning to shut out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bar someone is to exclude or throw them out.

clue.text: Hermia and Lysander?

parts.note: the two lovers form a pair, a team, in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: Just the names of two Shakespearean lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase usually means an ideal line-up; here it is read as a team found in the Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: the lovers are a duo from Shakespeare's Dream, and the idiom means a perfect group.

clue.text: Beginning of big article on old Scottish resort town

indicators.note: on means placed after, in an across clue, so the old letter comes first
beginning of takes just the opening letter of the word big

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a seaside town in Scotland in its heyday.
explanation.walkthrough: Oban is a harbour town on Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this west-coast harbour town is a holiday destination and ferry port in Scotland.

clue.text: All right following cheerful European song

indicators.note: following puts the agreement word after the other two pieces

parts.note: bright means cheerful or lively
yes is a way of saying all right, agreeing

explanation.surface: Someone approving after a happy European tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Bright Eyes is the Art Garfunkel hit from the film Watership Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a 1979 UK number one, sung by Art Garfunkel for an animated rabbit film.

clue.text: Fresh landlord brought round second bulletin

indicators.note: brought round says the landlord is moved round to follow the second

parts.note: new means fresh
a letter is one who lets property

explanation.surface: A new landlord comes round a second time to deliver a notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landlord' as 'one who lets' is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a regular printed or emailed update sent to members is a bulletin.

clue.text: Not working free

definitions.meaning: idle, without a job or task
vacant, available, as a seat or room

explanation.surface: Someone out of work and so at liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means idle, having nothing to do, and also vacant, as an empty seat that is free.

clue.text: Struggle with appearance

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

explanation.surface: Someone battling with how they look.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a view is a sight or appearance, how something looks to an observer.

clue.text: Intellectuals encourage one working in theatre?

parts.note: brains are clever people
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: Thinkers egging on an actor in a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre here is an operating theatre, not a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: a neurosurgeon works in an operating theatre, the hospital sense of the place.

clue.text: Grassland swamp associated with Alabama — Montgomery, for example

parts.note: a field is grassland
a marsh is a swamp
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: Geography notes on wet grassland near Montgomery, Alabama's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Montgomery looks like the Alabama city; it is the British WWII commander Bernard Montgomery.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Bernard Montgomery held Britain's highest army rank after leading at El Alamein.

clue.text: One's played card game in shady inlet

indicators.note: in puts the card game inside the reworked letters
shady means dubious or crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

parts.note: whist is a trick-taking card game

explanation.surface: A game of cards played in a shaded creek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shady' signals the anagram, giving TINLE; 'One's played' is the definition, read as 'a thing that is played'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the penny whistle is a simple instrument, so it is something that gets played.

clue.text: Designated route of escape that's on track

indicators.note: that's on puts the escape word on top of the track in a down entry

parts.note: flight is escape, fleeing
a path is a track

explanation.surface: A getaway plan that is going well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on track' reads as a phrase meaning going to plan, but 'track' alone is the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an aircraft's planned course through the air is a designated route.

clue.text: Unreadable? I'll say! Book one bishop rejected

parts.note: the contraction written without its apostrophe
e.g. means for example, i.e. say

indicators.note: rejected says one of the bishop letters is thrown out of the book

parts.note: the Bible is the Book
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop; the book has two, and one goes

explanation.surface: An exclamation of agreement, then something about a bishop turning a book down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say!' looks like an exclamation but gives EG; BIBLE losing one B leaves IBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: writing that cannot be deciphered is unreadable.

clue.text: Ashamed to make money playing sport

parts.note: to feel bad is to feel ashamed
to mint is to make coins
on means playing, being performed

explanation.surface: Someone embarrassed about earning from games.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a racket game played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Incompetent writer held back by it

indicators.note: held (by it) puts the writing tool inside the word it
back says the writer word is read in reverse

parts.note: a pen is a writer, a thing that writes

explanation.surface: An author being restrained by some unnamed thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PEN to NEP, which IT holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone clumsy and unskilled is incompetent.

clue.text: Bet women get on together, ultimately

parts.note: to age is to get on in years

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word together

explanation.surface: A gamble that the women will eventually be friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on' looks like 'be friendly'; it means grow older.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a wager is a stake placed on an outcome.

clue.text: Syrian in a public display of anger behind barrier

indicators.note: behind puts the scene after the barrier

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water
to make a scene is to show anger in public

explanation.surface: A Syrian throwing a tantrum behind a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Damascus is Syria's capital, so something from there is Syrian.

clue.text: Where to see film stars adequately briefed?

definitions.meaning: film actors appear on screen, in a motion picture

explanation.surface: A question about where celebrities are seen, and a note on being informed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means kept informed; literally, cinema actors are seen in a film.

clue.text: Robber, one arrested by the force

indicators.note: arrested by puts the one inside the word the, as if held

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: A criminal caught by the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the force' looks like the police; it splits into THE and F.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who steals is a robber.

clue.text: Striking leader of band, advanced in years

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of the word band

parts.note: old means advanced in years

explanation.surface: An elderly bandleader who cuts a fine figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bold design or colour is vivid and eye-catching.

clue.text: Refuse in study close to library

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

indicators.note: close to takes the end letter of the word library

explanation.surface: Rubbish found in a study near the library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like the noun meaning rubbish; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to refuse a request is to turn it down.

clue.text: Hook in role reversal

indicators.note: reversal says the role word is read backwards

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Captain Hook played in a role-swap production.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to hook a fish or a person is to catch or ensnare them.

clue.text: To achieve the intended effect, refuse to work in the house

parts.note: to strike is to stop work in protest
a home is a house

explanation.surface: Workers achieving their goal by staging a stay-at-home walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a blow or remark that lands with full force has its intended effect.

clue.text: Parrot or some screech owl

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A choice between two birds: a parrot or a screech owl.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Parrot or' as the definition; 'or' only joins the definition to the wordplay, so the definition is 'Parrot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to parrot words is to repeat them, as an echo does.

clue.text: Building in need of a yard, sooner or later

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters are assembled into something new

explanation.surface: A construction job that is short of a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' rearranges IN NEED OF A into ONEFINEDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase means at some unspecified time to come, eventually.
